tier_reason: Upgraded from C: an independent downstream project (flui, not linebender) measured parley against cosmic-text with a public harness (tools/text-spike/src/main.rs, parley_backend.rs, cosmic_backend.rs, scripts/run_measurements.sh at commit e30ab7194) and checked in the raw 240-point results/measurements.jsonl, from which the verifier recomputed every large-size median and ratio exactly (e.g. latin 4255 vs 781 ms, cjk 5120 vs 566 ms). Not A because the rustc version and exact CPU model are not stated (macOS on Apple Silicon only; release profile with debug = true).

corrections.baseline: cosmic-text 0.19.0 (pop-os/cosmic-text), the established Rust rich-text shaping and layout library (bevy_text, iced, COSMIC); both shape with HarfRust, but different versions: cosmic-text 0.19.0 pulls harfrust 0.5.2 while parley 0.11.1 pulls harfrust 0.12.0 (flui spike Cargo.lock). Not a C/C++ incumbent such as HarfBuzz with FreeType or Pango.
corrections.claimed_speedup: flui PR 1276 (merged 2026-09-23), docs/research/text-stack-2026.md, final (third) pass, 10,000-line documents, one parley Layout per paragraph, cold cache, median of 5 (cosmic-text vs parley): latin 4255 vs 781 ms (5.4x), arabic 3070 vs 1258 ms (2.4x), arabic_mixed 4474 vs 961 ms (4.7x), cjk 5120 vs 566 ms (9.0x), emoji_zwj 3083 vs 782 ms (3.9x), devanagari 3246 vs 1075 ms (3.0x): 2.4x-9.0x faster (the PR summary still quotes 2.4x-8.4x from an earlier pass), and 1.2x-4.2x less shaping-attributable memory. Single paragraph: warm 0.07-0.14 ms vs 0.32-0.49 ms, cold 6.1-6.6 ms vs 6.9-7.6 ms. When a whole document is handed to one parley Layout, parley is far slower (devanagari 10,000 lines: 78,782 ms vs cosmic-text 3,265 ms). massive PR 154 (merged 2026-09-15), docs/adr/0005-dual-shaping-engines-cosmic-text-and-parley.md (criterion, bundled JetBrains Mono 13 px, M-series Mac, warm cache): single ASCII cluster cosmic-text 1.8 us vs parley 2.1 us (cosmic-text ~16% faster); full mixed line parley 28 us vs cosmic-text 137 us (~4.8x); full-screen throughput parley ~2x; fallback stress parley ~2.7x; cold start with a fresh font database parley 61 us vs cosmic-text 36 ms (~600x in parley's favour, caused by cosmic-text's FontSystem construction).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: flui spike: cargo build --release (default release opt-level, [profile.release] debug = true), CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; rustc version not stated (crate MSRVs 1.88/1.89, flui workspace MSRV 1.97). massive: criterion, flags not stated.
corrections.hardware: flui PR 1276: macOS on Apple Silicon (arm64), a shared dev machine with no concurrent builds; exact chip not stated. massive PR 154: 'M-series Mac'.
corrections.workload: flui spike: shape and lay out six corpora (Latin, pure-RTL Arabic, Arabic plus Latin bidi, CJK, ZWJ emoji, Devanagari) as one short paragraph and as the paragraph repeated to 10,000 lines, cold and warm backend caches, 5 reps each, one process per run, requesting the SansSerif generic from macOS system fonts at 16 px with unbounded width (no --max-width, so no wrapping inside a line); parley 0.11.1 vs cosmic-text 0.19.0. massive: criterion terminal workloads (single cluster, full mixed line, 50-line full screen, fallback stress, cold start) with bundled JetBrains Mono 13 px.
corrections.caveats: Third-party measurements by two downstream projects (flui and massive), not by the Parley authors and not peer reviewed. Rust, so it does not match the catalog's default C++ language filter. Baseline cosmic-text is a recognisable Rust-ecosystem incumbent but not a C/C++ one (HarfBuzz with FreeType, Pango); the two libraries use different HarfRust versions (0.5.2 vs 0.12.0), so part of the gap may come from the newer shaper rather than Parley's own code. The flui harness lays out at unbounded width, so line wrapping is not exercised; it requests system fonts by generic family and did not check fallback quality (tofu glyphs would still count); glyph counts differ on emoji_zwj (-3.19%) and arabic_mixed (-0.25%). The flui PR, co-authored with an AI assistant, went through three correction rounds (a quadratic cost when the whole document is one parley Layout, 78,782 ms vs 3,265 ms on 10,000 Devanagari lines; a memory-retention asymmetry; mismatched font generics and a destruction boundary inside the timer); the earlier 30-38x memory figures are superseded. The massive benchmark source (mt benches/terminal_shaping.rs) was not found in the massive repository, and there cosmic-text wins the single-cluster hot path by about 16%. flui issue 931 relays an unaudited floem report of parley being '93% slower on Arabic wrap'. Neither measurement covers rasterization.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README 'How Does it Compare': 'rustybuzz-wasm would appear to be 1.5 times faster than harfbuzzjs', 'over 3 times faster than' opentype.js, 'over 12 times' the HarfBuzz command line. Introduction tables, 100 lines x 100 words, 65,732 items: rustybuzz_wasm_rusty_shaping 218,840 Hz vs harfbuzzjs_shaping 176,392 Hz (about 1.24x, derived from page data); bar-chart run 220,399 Hz vs 143,434 Hz (about 1.54x, derived from page data); harfbuzz_shaping (command line, one process per line) 17,553 Hz. A second 'Benchmarks' section without harfbuzzjs: 286,779 Hz vs opentype.js 61,997 Hz (1 / 4.6), fontkit 27,953 Hz (1 / 10.3), HarfBuzz command line 16,221 Hz (1 / 17.7).
corrections.caveats: WebAssembly versus WebAssembly: the comparable baseline, harfbuzzjs, is HarfBuzz's official WASM build (a recognisable incumbent, but not native HarfBuzz), and the 12x-17.7x figures are against the HarfBuzz command-line tool spawned once per line, which the author says 'does not tell you how fast HarfBuzz itself is'. Rust compiled to WASM, so it does not match the catalog's default C++ language filter. The benchmark (hengist textshaping.benchmarks.coffee) shapes Latin text in EBGaramond12-Italic.otf, counts text.length (UTF-16 code units, not glyphs), runs 3 shuffled repetitions, and calls rustybuzz-wasm with no OpenType features (lib.rs sets features to an empty list) and its 'rusty' serialized-string output, while the harfbuzzjs wrapper is handed a features object {liga, clig, dlig, hlig}; that wrapper (hengist apps/glyphshapes-and-typesetting-with-harfbuzz) was not found, so work parity and output format cannot be checked, though the README says harfbuzzjs then 'does not support font features'. In the current source the harfbuzzjs row is commented out, so the published harfbuzzjs numbers cannot be regenerated as is. The two published runs disagree (1.24x vs 1.54x). No CPU (a '2015 customer grade' laptop), Node.js version or build flags; README stresses release builds via wasm-pack. Uses rustybuzz 0.4 (2021), which predates HarfRust; behdad's 2025-09-10 note that HarfRust is within 25% of native HarfBuzz (1.06x on Roboto) concerns a later library. The LICENSE file is a placeholder, so usability stays reference. Last commit 2022-02-08; the README calls it a work in progress.

corrections.claimed_speedup: No Pretext-versus-DOM numbers in the repository. The current README says 'Fast, accurate' and that layout() is 'pure arithmetic. No DOM layout & reflow!'. Early README versions in the npm tarballs 0.0.0 to 0.0.4 (March-April 2026) gave first-party absolute timings with no DOM baseline: prepare() about 17-19 ms and layout() about 0.09-0.10 ms for a shared 500-text batch. Third-party blogs and landing pages (snippets only) call it '300-600x' or '500x faster' than DOM measurement; none of this is measured in the repo.
corrections.caveats: Tier D: no head-to-head DOM measurement table in README, RESEARCH.md, DEVELOPMENT.md, harness/README.md, pages/ or the early npm READMEs; the bun harness bench compares Pretext builds with each other. The baseline (browser DOM measurement via getBoundingClientRect/offsetHeight and the reflow they force) is the recognisable web-platform incumbent, but not a C/C++ library, and the project is TypeScript, so it does not match the catalog's default C++ language filter. The work differs from the baseline: prepare() still measures segments with the browser's Canvas text measurement, and layout() is arithmetic over cached widths, so a 'faster than DOM' figure compares a cached re-layout with a full style and layout pass. It measures and breaks lines; it does not shape glyphs, so HarfBuzz or FreeType are not comparable baselines. Included as a notable (50.7k stars) tier D entry.
